subject: Production latency + errors impacting reserved capacity — immediate triage
messages:
From: Simon Keller <simon.keller@novacorp.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-ops@novacorp.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Production — increased latency and 5xx from reserved deployment

Sergio,

We started seeing a steady increase in average token latency across our model endpoints at ~08:40 PT. Around 09:00 we began getting intermittent 5xx errors for user-facing requests; roughly 1.8% error rate now (was ~0.1% baseline). Our monitoring shows queued requests and timeouts against the reserved GPU pool. This is impacting our user sessions.

Can you confirm whether this is a configuration issue on our side or a capacity problem on Redwood's dedicated pool? We rely on the reserved throughput commitment for peak hours and customers are already noticing degradation.

I've attached a short error log extract and a couple of request IDs for quick lookup.

Attachment: error_snippet.txt (plain text)

Thanks — please escalate if needed.

— Simon
Platform Ops, NovaCorp

On Mon, May 11, 2026 at 09:22 AM, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Initial ask: Irene, can your team post a brief occupancy snapshot and confirm whether any recent rollout touched the customer's pinned model variant in the reserved pool?

Quick triage notes (attached snapshot + short summary):
- Observed sustained 96–98% GPU utilization on the customer's reserved nodes between 08:35–09:10 PT.
- Queue depth (requests waiting for GPU slots) increased ~6x versus baseline.
- KV cache eviction rate spiked; prefix cache misses increased latency for warm-start flows.
- No model rollout recorded for the customer's pinned version in the last 24h.
- There was an automated global scale decision that briefly rebalanced capacity; it appears that the customer's dedicated pool received lower headroom as a side effect of a non-blocking autoscaler adjustment for a different AZ.

Immediate mitigations applied at 10:00 PT (partial):
- Reduced per-request batch size for NovaCorp routes (temporary config override) — lowered 95th p90 token latency by ~160ms in testing.
- Enabled fallback routing to the compatible hosted variant for non-critical flows (CS-only endpoints).
- Increased preemptible burst allocation for 15 minutes to drain queue.

Attachments: pool-occupancy-20260511.png (PNG)

Recommended next steps:
- Exec sync with Redwood leadership to confirm reserve isolation policy and to decide on compensation/credits.
- Post-mortem to review autoscaler decision boundary that caused headroom bleed.

I will keep live metrics on the Alert dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/alerts/novacorp-queue-depth

— Irene
Ops Lead, Dedicated Services

1) Quick decision on whether to temporarily migrate some of their critical routes to hosted capacity (with a short-term uplift) while we restore isolation guarantees.
2) Guidance on credits/contract remedies — early estimate attached (cost-analysis.xlsx).
3) Exec presence for a 3pm PT sync (CTO + Head of Product + Ops) to approve immediate remediation and external comms.

Simon, appreciate your patience. We will be transparent about actions and timing.

— Priyom
